title: Inspect and extend: Render navigation through WebKit
objective: Use the real implementation in `Sources/WebView.swift` to demonstrate and safely improve representable wrapper, load calls, and browser controls.
problem: The app’s native controls sit around a WebKit page. Follow a selected URL into the wrapper and understand which behavior is delegated to Apple’s WebKit engine. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `Sources/WebView.swift` and the related project files: Sources/WebView.swift; Sources/Screens/BrowserScreen.swift.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to representable wrapper, load calls, and browser controls.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: The project does not embed Firefox’s Gecko engine.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: The app’s native controls sit around a WebKit page. Follow a selected URL into the wrapper and understand which behavior is delegated to Apple’s WebKit engine.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `Sources/WebView.swift`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
